paragraphs: The accompanying combined and consolidated financial statements include the combined and consolidated results of operations of Jefferson Capital, Inc., and its subsidiaries (the "Company"). Jefferson Capital, Inc. is a Delaware corporation headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

The Company and its subsidiaries in the U.S., Canada, the U.K and Latin America, provide debt recovery solutions and other related services across a broad range of consumer receivables, including credit card, secured and unsecured automotive, utilities, telecom, and other receivables. The Company primarily purchases portfolios of consumer receivables at deep discounts to face value and manages them by working with individuals as they repay their obligations and work toward financial recovery. Previously charged-off receivables include receivables subject to bankruptcy proceedings. The Company also provides debt servicing and other portfolio management services to credit originators for non-performing loans. Through credit card acquisition programs, the Company earns credit card revenue. All deployments are purchased from independent third parties.

The Company purchases portfolios of receivables from a diverse client base, including Fortune 500 creditors, banks, fintech origination platforms, telecommunications providers, credit card issuers, and auto finance companies. The Company's top five clients accounted for 45.2% and 55.3%, with the top client representing 23.6% and 32.8% of purchases for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. For credit card receivables, the Company purchases from two issuers.

In June 2025, the Company completed its initial public offering ("IPO"), in which the selling shareholders sold 10,875,000 shares after giving effect to the underwriters' exercise of the over-allotment option, at a public offering price of $15.00 per share. The Company also issued and sold 625,000 shares of its common stock in the IPO, which resulted in net proceeds of $4.5 million after deducting the underwriting discounts and commissions. Prior to the IPO, our business operations were generally conducted through Jefferson Capital Holdings, LLC, and its subsidiaries. JCAP TopCo, LLC is a holding company and the direct parent of Jefferson Capital Holdings, LLC. JCAP TopCo, LLC was owned by (i) entities affiliated with J.C. Flowers, (ii) members of Management Invest, LLC, and (iii) former equity holders of Canaccede Financial Group, Ltd. ("Canaccede").

Following a series of transactions that we refer to collectively as the "Reorganization," Jefferson Capital, Inc. became a holding company with no material assets other than 100% of the equity interests in JCAP TopCo, LLC, which is held by Jefferson Capital, Inc. both directly and indirectly through other wholly-owned holding companies that have no material assets other than direct or indirect equity interests in JCAP TopCo, LLC. JCAP TopCo, LLC remains a holding company with no material assets other than 100% of the equity interests in Jefferson Capital Holdings, LLC. Jefferson Capital, Inc. also succeeded to federal Net Operating Losses (NOLs), state NOLs and tax credit carryforwards under Section 381 of the Code as a result of its acquisition in the Reorganization of certain affiliated corporations that held direct or indirect equity interests in JCAP TopCo, LLC. As indirect parent of Jefferson Capital Holdings, LLC, following the Reorganization, Jefferson Capital, Inc. operates and controls all of the business and affairs, and consolidates the financial results of, Jefferson Capital Holdings, LLC, and its subsidiaries. To effect the Reorganization, the then-current direct and indirect owners of JCAP TopCo, LLC, including (i) entities affiliated with J.C. Flowers, (ii) members of Management Invest, LLC, an entity through which employees of JCAP TopCo, LLC and its subsidiaries and certain of our directors held equity interests, and (iii) former equity holders of Canaccede, exchanged their direct and indirect interests in JCAP TopCo, LLC for shares of our common stock. We refer to the entities affiliated with J.C. Flowers, members of Management Invest, LLC and former stockholders of Canaccede who own shares of our common stock following the Reorganization and the IPO as the "JCF Stockholders," "Management Stockholders" and "Former Canaccede Stockholders," respectively. As a result of the Reorganization and after giving effect to the completion of the IPO at the initial public offering price of $15.00 per share, as of December 31, 2025:
● the investors in the IPO collectively own 18.1% of our common stock;

● the JCF Stockholders collectively own 67.6% of the outstanding shares of our common stock. Following quarter end, we executed a follow-on equity offering, which reduced the ownership of JCF Stockholders to 53.1%. The company repurchased $58.9 million of stock to support that transaction;
● the Management Stockholders collectively own 14.3%;

● The number of shares of common stock received by the JCF Stockholders, the Former Canaccede Stockholders and the Management Stockholders in exchange for the 132,828,019 Class A Units and Class C Units of JCAP TopCo, LLC outstanding immediately prior to the Reorganization was based on an exchange ratio of one share of our common stock for every 2.4150549 interests in JCAP TopCo, LLC (the "Exchange Ratio"), resulting in an aggregate of 55,000,000 shares of our common stock being issued in exchange for such Class A Units and Class C units.

In addition, based on the initial public offering price of $15.00 per share, an aggregate of 9,060,082 shares of common stock were issued in exchange for the 27,937,232 Class B Units of JCAP TopCo, LLC outstanding immediately prior to the Reorganization, resulting in a total of 64,060,082 shares of common stock outstanding immediately after the Reorganization and before giving effect to the IPO. The number of shares of common stock that the Management Stockholders collectively received pursuant to the Reorganization was based in part on the value that Management Invest, LLC would have received under the distribution provisions of the limited liability agreement of JCAP TopCo, LLC, with shares of our common stock valued by reference to the ultimate initial public offering price of shares of common stock in the IPO. Specifically, of the 9,060,082 shares of common stock issued to the Management Stockholders in the Reorganization, 6,418,775 shares were issued in respect of Class B Units of Management Invest, LLC (which correspond to Class B Units of JCAP TopCo, LLC) that are "in- the-money" but remain subject to certain vesting conditions specified in individual award agreements. These shares were issued as restricted stock either with the same time-based vesting requirements that the corresponding Class B Units were subject to prior to the Reorganization or, if such corresponding Class B Units had performance vesting requirements, with a three year time-vesting requirement. If the vesting conditions of the restricted stock are not satisfied, such restricted stock will be forfeited and canceled.

We purchase portfolios of nonperforming loans, and occasionally those that are performing but with significant credit deterioration, through either single portfolio transactions, referred to as spot sales, or through the pre-arranged purchase of multiple portfolios at regular intervals, referred to as forward flow sales. Under a forward flow contract, we agree to purchase statistically similar nonperforming loan portfolios from credit grantors on a periodic basis at a pre-negotiated price over a specified time period, generally from six months to a year.

When we purchase portfolios with credit deterioration, we find that our expertise in evaluating and managing charged-off accounts allows us to confidently manage such portfolios with a higher level of credit risk than a buyer without that level of expertise would be comfortable. In such instances, a portfolio may include a mix of loans that are delinquent and restructured as well as a significant amount of charged-off or nonperforming loans, as was the case with the Conn's Portfolio, and with a high level of risk that more of the current loans will become delinquent over time and eventually need to be charged-off. In these cases, we can offer the seller the convenience of purchasing all its loan assets together as opposed to bidding for only a single category of loan, which might result in a seller needing to transact with multiple counterparties. We regularly evaluate the opportunity to purchase portfolios that include a mix of performing accounts and nonperforming accounts, and that comprise all of a credit originator's loan assets and believe we will find attractive opportunities to make more purchases like these going forward.

We purchase portfolios of nonperforming loans from credit grantors through auctions and negotiated sales. In an auction process, the seller will assemble a portfolio of nonperforming loans and will seek purchase prices from specifically invited potential purchasers. In a privately negotiated sale process, the seller will contact one or more purchasers directly, receive a bid, and negotiate the terms of sale. In either case, invited purchasers will typically have already successfully completed a qualification process and due diligence examination that includes the seller's review of the purchaser's experience, financial standing, operating procedures, business practices, and compliance oversight.

We purchase receivables based on robust, account-level valuation methods and employ proprietary statistical and behavioral models across our operations. These methods and models allow us to value portfolios accurately (and limit the risk of overpaying), avoid buying portfolios that are incompatible with our methods or strategies, and align the accounts we purchase with our business and collection channels to maximize future collections. As a result, we have been able to realize attractive returns from the receivables we acquire. We maintain strong relationships with many of the largest financial service providers in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom and Latin America.

Risks Related to Our International Operations
Our international operations expose us to risks, which could harm our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Compliance with complex and evolving international and U.S. laws and regulations that apply to our international operations could increase our cost of doing business in international jurisdictions.
Risks Related to Government Regulation and Litigation
Our ability to collect and enforce our nonperforming and performing loans may be limited under federal, state and international laws, regulations and policies.

Failure to comply with government regulation of the collections industry could result in penalties, fines, litigation, damage to our reputation or the suspension or termination of our ability to conduct our business.
Changes in tax provisions or exposures to additional tax liabilities could have an adverse tax effect on our financial condition.
Recent changes in U.S. trade policy could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Risks Related to Information Technology, Cybersecurity and Intellectual Property
We are dependent on our data gathering systems and proprietary consumer profiles, and if access to such data was lost or became public, our business could be materially and adversely affected.
We and our third-party providers are exposed to cybersecurity risks and incidents which could damage our reputation and adversely impact our business and financial results.

The underperformance or failure of our information technology infrastructure, networks or communication systems could result in a loss in productivity, loss of competitive advantage and business disruption.
We may not be able to adequately protect the intellectual property rights upon which we rely and, as a result, any lack of protection may diminish our competitive advantage.
Risks Related to Our Financial Condition and Indebtedness
We expect to use leverage in executing our business strategy, which may have adverse consequences.
paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below and the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K before making an investment in our common stock. Our business, financial condition, results of operations, or prospects could be materially and adversely affected if any of these risks occurs, and as a result, the market price of our common stock could decline and you could lose all or part of your investment. This Annual Report on Form 10-K also contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. See "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements." Our actual results could differ materially and adversely from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of certain factors, including those set forth below.

Our performance may be adversely affected by economic, political or inflationary conditions in any market in which we operate. These conditions could include regulatory developments, changes in global or domestic economic policy, legislative changes, and sovereign debt crises. Deterioration in economic conditions, or a significant rise in inflation or high level of sustained inflation could negatively affect the ability of consumers to pay their debts and could reduce the real value of our purchased receivables. This may in turn adversely impact our business and financial results.

If global credit market conditions and the stability of global banks deteriorate, the amount of consumer or commercial lending and financing could be reduced, thus reducing the volume of nonperforming loans available for purchase, which could adversely affect our business, financial results and ability to succeed in the markets in which we operate. Uncertainty about future economic conditions, including the possibility of a recession, a disease outbreak and impacts from wars, such as in Ukraine and in the Middle East makes it difficult for us to forecast operating results and to make decisions about future investments.

Other economic factors that could influence our performance include the financial stability of the lenders on our Revolving Credit Facility (as defined herein) and our access to capital and credit. For example, deterioration in the financial markets could contribute to the insolvency of lending institutions, notably those providing our Revolving Credit Facility, or the tightening of credit markets, which could make it difficult or impossible for us to obtain credit on favorable terms or at all. These and other economic factors could have an adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.

We may not be able to continually replace our nonperforming loans with additional portfolios sufficient to operate efficiently and profitably, and/or we may not be able to purchase nonperforming loans at appropriate prices.

To operate profitably, we must purchase and service a sufficient amount of nonperforming loans to generate revenue that exceeds our expenses. Salaries and other compensation expense constitute a significant portion of our operating expenses and, if we do not replace the nonperforming loan portfolios we service with additional portfolios, we may have to reduce the number of our collection and other administrative personnel. paragraphs: MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

You should read the following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations in conjunction with the combined and consolidated financial statements and the related notes and other financial data included elsewhere in the Annual Report on Form 10-K. In addition to historical financial information, the following discussion contains forward-looking statements that reflect our plans, estimates, beliefs, and expectations that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results and the timing of events could differ materially from those discussed in the forward-looking statements. Factors that could cause or contribute to these differences include those discussed below and the sections titled "Risk Factors" and "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" in this Annual Report on Form 10-K (the "Annual Report"). A discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the year ended December 31, 2023 is included under "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in our final prospectus filed with the SEC pursuant to Rule 424(b)(4) on June 27, 2025.

We provide debt recovery solutions and other related services across a broad range of consumer receivables, including credit card, secured and unsecured automotive, telecom and utilities, and other receivables. We primarily purchase portfolios of previously charged-off consumer receivables at deep discounts to face value and manage them by working with individuals as they repay their obligations and work toward financial recovery. Previously charged-off receivables include receivables subject to bankruptcy proceedings. We also provide debt servicing and other portfolio management services to credit originators for nonperforming loans. In addition, through our credit card acquisition programs, we earn credit card revenue. All deployments are made to independent third parties.

We operate and manage our business through four reportable segments that are based on geography: United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Latin America. We also have the following two primary lines of business:
◾ Distressed, our largest line of business, represents the purchase, collection, and servicing collection of nonperforming consumer loans; and

◾ Insolvency, which consists of the purchasing and/or servicing of financial assets of consumers who have entered bankruptcy through Chapter 7 or 13 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code in the United States, consumer proposal, credit counseling, or bankruptcy in Canada and the United Kingdom.
We are headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, and as of December 31, 2025, with 1,120 FTE (including our offshore co-sourced operation).

We regularly review net operating income and net income along with a number of key business metrics and non-GAAP financial measures to evaluate our business, measure our performance, identify trends, prepare financial projections, and make business decisions. Although we believe the key business metrics and non-GAAP financial measures we review are useful, they have limitations as analytical tools and should not be considered in isolation, or as substitutes for analysis of our financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP.

We define ERC as the undiscounted sum of all future projected collections on our owned finance receivables portfolios. We calculate ERC using data derived from our databases of owned and serviced debt portfolio in the markets in which we operate and from our proprietary behavioral and asset valuation models. References to our ERC are references to gross ERC (which includes estimated collections in respect of the current charge-off balances). We believe that our ERC estimation represents an important supplemental measure to compare our cash generating capacity with other companies in the debt collection industry, even though we can provide no assurance that we will achieve such collections within a specified time period, or at all.

附屬之合併及合併財務報表包含Jefferson Capital, Inc.及其子公司（"本公司"）之合併及合併營運結果。Jefferson Capital, Inc.為設立於明尼蘇達州 Minneapolis 的德拉瓦州公司。

本公司及其在美國、加拿大、英國及拉丁美洲之子公司，提供債務回收解決方案及其他相關服務，服務範圍涵蓋廣泛之消費者應收款，包括信用卡、有擔保及無擔保汽車貸款、電力、電信業者及其他應收款。本公司主要以低於面值的折扣價格購買消費者應收款組合，並透過協助個人償還債務及朝向財務復原來管理這些應收款。先前已核銷之應收款包括遭動議破產程序之應收款。本公司亦為信貸發行機構提供債務管理及其他組合管理服務，針對不良貸款。透過信用卡取得計畫，本公司賺取信用卡收入。所有部署均從獨立第三方購買。
本公司從多樣化之客戶羣購買應收款組合，包括財富500大債權人、銀行、金融科技發行平台、電信業者、信用卡發卡機構及汽車貸款公司。本公司前五大客戶於2025年12月31日財年及2024年12月31日財年分別佔購入應收款之45.2%及55.3%，其中最大客戶分別佔購入應收款之23.6%及32.8%。針對信用卡應收款，本公司從兩家發卡機構購買。

2025年6月，本公司完成首次公開發行（"IPO"），在考慮到經理人行使過量發行權後，出售10,875,000股，發行價格為每股15.00美元。本公司亦在IPO中發行並出售625,000股普通股，扣除經理人折扣及佣金後，淨資金為4.5百萬美元。IPO前，本公司業務主要透過Jefferson Capital Holdings, LLC及其子公司進行。JCAP TopCo, LLC為控股公司，為Jefferson Capital Holdings, LLC之直接母公司。JCAP TopCo, LLC由（i）與J.C. Flowers有關聯之實體、（ii）Management Invest, LLC之成員，以及（iii）Canaccede Financial Group, Ltd.（"Canaccede"）之前股東所擁有。

透過一系列我們稱為"重組"之交易，Jefferson Capital, Inc.成為一家無重大資產之控股公司，僅持有JCAP TopCo, LLC 100%之權益利益，該權益利益由Jefferson Capital, Inc.直接及間接透過其他無重大資產之控股公司持有，這些控股公司僅持有JCAP TopCo, LLC之直接或間接權益利益。JCAP TopCo, LLC仍為一家無重大資產之控股公司，僅持有Jefferson Capital Holdings, LLC 100%之權益利益。Jefferson Capital, Inc.亦因重組中取得某些相關公司之權益利益，而繼承美國淨營業虧損（NOLs）、州級NOLs及稅務信用結轉權益。作為Jefferson Capital Holdings, LLC之間接母公司，重組後，Jefferson Capital, Inc.經營並控制Jefferson Capital Holdings, LLC及其子公司之所有業務及事務，並合併其財務結果。為實現重組，當時JCAP TopCo, LLC之直接及間接所有者，包括（i）與J.C. Flowers有關聯之實體、（ii）Management Invest, LLC之成員，該實體為JCAP TopCo, LLC及其子公司員工及部分董事所持有權益之實體，以及（iii）Canaccede之前股東，將其在JCAP TopCo, LLC之直接及間接權益換為本公司普通股。我們稱這些與J.C. Flowers有關聯之實體、Management Invest, LLC之成員及Canaccede之前股東，於重組及IPO後持有本公司普通股者為"JCF股東"、"管理股東"及"前Canaccede股東"。因重組，並考慮到IPO完成後以每股15.00美元之發行價格，截至2025年12月31日：
● IPO投資者 collectively 擁有本公司普通股之18.1%；
● JCF股東 collectively 擁有本公司普通股之67.6%。於季度結算後，我們執行追加股票發行，使JCF股東持股降至53.1%。公司購回58.9百萬美元股票以支持此交易；
● 管理股東 collectively 擁有14.3%；

● 本公司普通股股數係根據 JCAP TopCo, LLC 重整前現行的 132,828,019 筆 Class A 與 Class C 單元，按每 2.4150549 筆 JCAP TopCo, LLC 單元換發 1  shares of our common stock 的交換比例（"交換比例"）計算，因此總計發行 55,000,000 shares of our common stock 用以交換該等 Class A 與 Class C 單元。

此外，根據首次公開發行價格每 share $15.00，總計發行 9,060,082 shares of common stock 用以交換重整前現行的 27,937,232 筆 Class B 單元，因此重整後且尚未考慮 IPO 前，總計發行 64,060,082 shares of common stock。管理人股東根據重整所取得的普通股股數，部分係根據 Management Invest, LLC 在 JCAP TopCo, LLC 有限責任協議分紅條款下應得之價值計算，並以 IPO 最終首次公開發行價格作為本公司普通股之價值參考。具體而言，於重整中發行給管理人股東的 9,060,082 shares of common stock 中，6,418,775 shares 是為 Management Invest, LLC 的 Class B 單元（對應 JCAP TopCo, LLC 的 Class B 單元）發行，該等 Class B 單元為 "in-the-money" 但仍受個別獎勵契約中所規定的某些行權條件限制。這些股份是以限制性股票方式發行，其行權條件與重整前對應的 Class B 單元相同，若對應的 Class B 單元有績效行權條件，則以三年時間行權條件為準。若限制性股票之行權條件未達成，則該等限制性股票將被註銷。
我們透過單筆貸款組合交易（稱為 spot sales）或預先安排的定期購買多筆貸款組合（稱為 forward flow sales）方式，購買不良貸款組合，有時也包括表現良好但信用狀況惡化的貸款組合。在 forward flow 合約下，我們同意在指定時間內，以預先協議的價格，定期購買信用授予人提供的統計上相似的不良貸款組合，通常為六個月至一年的時間範圍。

當我們購買信用狀況惡化的貸款組合時，我們的專業評估與管理已核銷帳戶的能力，使我們能以較高信用風險的組合進行管理，這對缺乏此專業能力的買家而言可能不具備足夠的信心。在這些情況下，組合可能包含逾期與重整貸款，以及大量已核銷或不良貸款，如 Conn's Portfolio 的情況，且風險較高，未來可能有更多貸款成為逾期，最終需進行核銷。在這些情況下，我們可以為賣方提供將所有貸款資產一併購買的便利，而非僅競標某一類貸款，這可能導致賣方需與多個對手進行交易。我們定期評估購買包含表現良好與不良帳戶混合組合的貸款組合機會，並認為未來將持續發現具吸引力的購入機會。
我們透過拍賣與協議銷售方式，從信用授予人處購買不良貸款組合。在拍賣程序中，賣方會組建不良貸款組合，並向特定邀請的潛在買家尋求購買價格。在私下協議銷售程序中，賣方會直接聯繫一個或多個買家，接收報價，並協議銷售條款。在任一種情況下，受邀買家通常已成功完成資格審查與盡職調查，包括賣方對買家經驗、財務狀況、作業程序、商業作風及合規監督的審查。
我們根據強大的帳戶層面評估方法購買應收款，並在整個運營中運用專利的統計與行為模型。這些方法與模型使我們能準確評估組合（並限制過度支付的風險），避免購買與我們方法或策略不兼容的組合，並使我們購買的帳戶與業務及收款渠道對應，以最大化未來收款。因此，我們已能從所購入的應收款中實現有吸引力的回報。我們與美國、加拿大、英國及拉丁美洲的許多大型金融服務提供商維持良好的關係。

paragraphs: 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析

您應配合本公司的合併財務報表與相關附註及其他財務資料，一併閱讀以下對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析。除歷史財務資訊外，以下討論包含向前看的陳述，反映本公司之計畫、預估、信念與預期，這些陳述涉及風險與不確定性。本公司實際結果與事件發生時間可能與向前看陳述中所討論者有重大差異。造成或導致這些差異的因素包括以下所討論之內容，以及本年度報表（Form 10-K）中標題為「風險因素」與「向前看陳述之警示」之部分。有關本公司 2024 年 12 月 31 日財務狀況與營運成果與 2023 年 12 月 31 日之比較之討論，包含於本年度報表（Form 10-K）中標題為「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」之部分，該部分為本公司於 2025 年 6 月 27 日依 Rule 424(b)(4) 向 SEC 提交之最終發行說明書。

我們提供債務回收解決方案及其他相關服務，服務範圍涵蓋廣泛之消費者應收款，包括信用卡、有擔保與無擔保汽車貸款、電信與公用事業，以及其他應收款。我們主要以遠低於面值的價格購買已遭核銷之消費者應收款組合，並透過與個人合作償還義務及朝向財務復原來管理這些應收款。已遭核銷之應收款包括遭動產清算程序處理之應收款。我們也為信貸發行機構提供債務服務及其他組合管理服務，針對非表現貸款。此外，透過我們之信用卡採購計畫，我們賺取信用卡收入。所有部署均針對獨立第三方進行。
我們透過四個應報告分部來運作與管理業務，這些分部依據地理區域劃分：美國、英國、加拿大與拉丁美洲。我們也擁有以下兩大主要業務線：
◾ Distressed，為我們最大之業務線，代表購買、回收與管理非表現消費者貸款；
◾ Insolvency，包含購買與/或管理美國根據美國破產法第 7 章或第 13 章進入破產程序之消費者財產，加拿大與英國之消費者提案、信貸諮詢或破產程序。
我們總部設於明尼蘇達州明尼阿波利斯市，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，擁有 1,120 名全職等效員工（包含我們之離岸共源作業）。
我們定期審閱淨營運收入與淨收入，以及多項關鍵業務指標與非 GAAP 財務指標，以評估業務、衡量表現、識別趨勢、準備財務預測並做出業務決策。雖然我們認為所審閱之關鍵業務指標與非 GAAP 財務指標是有用的，但它們作為分析工具有其限制，不應孤立看待，也不應作為依 GAAP 製作財務結果分析之替代。

我們將 ERC 定義為所有未來預期收款的未折現總和，針對我們所持有的財務應收款 portfolios。我們使用來自我們在營運市場所擁有及管理的債務 portfolios 資料庫，以及我們專有的行為與資產評價模型所衍生的資料來計算 ERC。提及我們的 ERC 時，指的是未扣除的 ERC（包含對當前核銷餘額的預估收款）。我們認為，我們的 ERC 預估是比較我們現金產生能力與債務回收行業其他公司的重要補充指標，儘管我們無法保證能在指定時間內或任何時候實現這些收款。

我們美國應報告分部的 ERC 包含來自 Conn's Portfolio 購買的 139.9 百萬美元，以及來自 Bluestem portfolio 購買的 295.6 百萬美元。
Deployments 指的是在正常業務過程中進行的 portfolios 購買。我們認為 Deployments 是衡量我們投資活動的重要指標。Deployments 是我們 ERC 成長的主要驅動因素，也是比較我們業務成長與債務回收行業其他公司成長的重要指標。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們營運國家的總體經濟或通貨膨脹環境惡化，可能對我們的業務及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們可能無法從非 Performing 貸款中收取足夠金額以支應營運資金。
若某些類型的破產程序及破產申報涉及清算的情況增加，我們的收款可能會減少。
我們在孟買的共源運作若發生中斷，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
商譽減損費用可能對我們的淨收入及股東權益產生負面影響。
我們的損失備抵準備金可能不足以覆蓋實際損失。
與我們國際營運相關的風險
本公司之國際業務使我們面臨風險，這些風險可能對我們之業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成損害。
遵守複雜且不斷演進之國際及美國法律與法規，可能增加我們在國際司法管轄區從事業務之成本。
與政府監管及訴訟相關之風險
本公司在美國聯邦、州及國際法律、法規及政策下，可能受限於追收及執行我們之不良貸款及正常貸款之能力。
未能遵守對貸款回收業之政府監管，可能導致處罰、罰款、訴訟、聲譽受損或暫停或終止我們從事業務之能力。
稅務規定之變更或對額外稅務負擔之暴露，可能對我們之財務狀況產生不利之稅務影響。
近期美國貿易政策之變更，可能對我們之業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
與資訊科技、網路安全及智慧財產權相關之風險
本公司依賴資料蒐集系統及專屬消費者資料檔案，若無法取得或資料公開，將可能對本公司業務造成重大且不利的影響。
本公司及其第三方服務提供者面臨網路安全風險及事件，可能損害本公司聲譽，並對業務及財務結果造成不利影響。
本公司資訊科技基礎建設、網路或通訊系統表現不佳或故障，可能導致生產力下降、競爭優勢喪失及業務中斷。
本公司可能無法充分保護所依賴的智慧財產權，因此若缺乏保護，可能削弱本公司競爭優勢。
與本公司財務狀況及負債相關的風險
本公司預期在執行業務策略時使用槓桿，這可能產生不利後果。
paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股涉及高度風險。您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，以及本年度報告表10-K所包含的其他資訊，再做投資本公司普通股的決定。若任何上述風險發生，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果或前景造成重大且不利的影響，進而導致本公司普通股市價下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。本年度報告表10-K亦包含涉及風險與不確定性的展望性陳述。請參閱「關於展望性陳述的特別說明」。本公司實際結果可能與這些展望性陳述所預期的有重大且不利的差異，原因在於某些因素，包括下列所列因素。
本公司營運表現可能因我們營運市場的經濟、政治或通貨膨脹條件而受到不利影響。這些條件可能包括法規發展、全球或國內經濟政策的變動、立法變更，以及國家債務危機。經濟條件惡化，或通貨膨脹顯著上升或高水準持續通貨膨脹，可能影響消費者償還債務的能力，並降低我們購入的應收款之實際價值。這可能會進一步對我們的業務與財務結果造成不利影響。
若全球信貸市場條件與全球銀行的穩定性惡化，消費者或商業貸款與融資的數量可能減少，進而減少可供購入的不良貸款數量，這可能對我們的業務、財務結果與在營運市場的競爭力造成不利影響。對未來經濟條件的不確定性，包括經濟衰退、疾病爆發以及戰爭（如烏克蘭與中東地區）的影響，使我們難以預測營運結果，並做出未來投資的決策。
其他可能影響我們營運表現的經濟因素包括我們循環信貸協議（如本文件所定義）中貸款人的財務穩定性，以及我們取得資金與信貸的可及性。例如，財務市場惡化可能導致貸款機構（特別是提供我們循環信貸協議的機構）的破產，或信貸市場收緊，這可能使我們難以以有利條件或完全無法取得信貸。這些及其他經濟因素可能對我們的財務狀況與營運結果產生不利影響。
我們可能無法持續以足夠的組合替換我們的不良貸款，以確保營運效率與獲利，且/或我們可能無法以適當價格購入不良貸款。
要營運獲利，我們必須購入並服務足夠數量的不良貸款，以產生的收入超過我們的費用。薪資及其他薪資支出佔我們營運費用的很大一部分，若我們無法以新組合替換我們服務的不良貸款組合，我們可能必須減少我們的催收及其他行政人員人數。我們隨後若取得新組合，可能必須重新僱用員工。這些做法可能導致負面後果，包括以下內容：
